title: When the Rain Stops
logline: In an eastern dry-zone village, the paddy comes up green and full, and then the rain that should keep coming simply stops.
human_question: What does a community do while it waits to find out whether this season will be the one that breaks it?

premise.story: A farming community around a large dry-zone tank, watching a promising crop as the rains fail, and making the hard daily decisions that follow.
premise.place: A tank-irrigated farming area in the Eastern Province dry zone.
premise.experience: A green, hopeful field turning to cracked earth, farmers checking the tank's water line each morning, and a community's practical response, water-sharing meetings, decisions about what to save.

concept_links.why: The source's account of how a world ends begins with something entirely ordinary: rain falls, people sow happily, the crop grows, and then the rain stops for good [C052-P:L156-L160]. A real drought carries that shape without any cosmic frame ever being spoken.

what_camera_could_observe: Farmers checking the tank's falling water line
A household's decision about what to save or let go
what_must_be_real: A real, current drought's real stakes for a real farming community. The film does not stage or predict the outcome.

possible_arc.opening: A full tank, a healthy crop.
possible_arc.turn: The rains fail to come; the water line keeps dropping.
possible_arc.ending_open: Whatever the community's season actually brings, a partial harvest, a hard decision, or rain arriving late.

requirements: A dry-zone tank-irrigated farming community currently facing or recently through a drought
Farmers and a water-management body willing to be filmed

suggestions.name: The Ampara or Batticaloa district dry zone
suggestions.why: Large tank-irrigated paddy areas in the eastern dry zone; suggested for regional variety alongside the group's other dry-zone stories.
suggestions.verify: No specific tank or village identified; current drought conditions would need confirming at the time of filming.

risks: Implying that drought is caused by anyone's moral failure
Turning real hardship into an apocalyptic metaphor
Suggesting fatalism about climate and livelihood
drop_if: No drought or water crisis is actually underway when filming would occur
No farming community consents to being filmed through a hard season

connections.note: A second growing-season story, this one following a community through a season's failure rather than a single family's.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: All content is editorial proposal. Location suggestions are AI suggestions only; selection belongs to Chathura.
